info.name: nestjs-rest-template
info.description:
REST API for nestjs-rest-template.

Run the whole collection in order (Collection Runner): **Auth → Login** stores `accessToken`, and **Users → Get users** stores `userId` for the requests after it. **Article categories → List article categories** stores `categoryId`, and **Articles → Create article** stores `articleId` / `articleSlug`; the Articles folder deletes the article it creates.

Default values match the local `.env` (`ADMIN_EMAIL` / `ADMIN_PASSWORD`) and the default port 3000.

The **Registration** folder creates a new `postman-<timestamp>@example.com` user on every run.

The same API is documented in Swagger UI at `{{baseUrl}}/docs`; `swagger/openapi.json` in the repo can also be imported into Postman.

`/auth/resend-verification` and `/auth/forgot-password` allow 3 requests per minute per IP, so wait a minute (or restart the API) before running the whole collection again.

item.name: Registration
item.description:
Register → (verify email) → login.

The verification link is written to the API log by `MailService`. Copy the `token` from it into the `verificationToken` collection variable to run **Verify email** and **Login after verification**; without it those tests are skipped.

exec: pm.test('Explains the conflict', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().message).to.eql('An account with this email already exists'));
pm.expect(messages).to.include('password must be longer than or equal to 8 characters');
pm.expect(messages).to.include('phoneNumber must be in international format, e.g. +994501234567');
pm.expect(messages).to.include('gender must be one of the following values: MALE, FEMALE');
pm.test('Rejects unknown fields', () => pm.expect(messages).to.include('property isAdmin should not exist'));
pm.test('Asks to verify the email', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().message).to.eql('Email is not verified'));

item.name: Verify email - access token is rejected

exec: pm.test('Rejects tokens issued for another purpose', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().message).to.eql('Token is invalid or has expired'));
pm.test.skip('Set verificationToken from the verification email in the API log', () => {});
pm.test('Same response as a registered email', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().sent).to.eql(true));

item.name: Password reset
item.description:
Forgot password → reset password → login with the new password, for the account created in **Registration**.

The reset link is written to the API log by `MailService`. Copy the `token` from it into the `resetToken` collection variable to run the last three requests; without it those tests are skipped. A reset link works only once.

exec: pm.test('Same response as a registered email', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().sent).to.eql(true));
pm.test('Rejects the token format', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().message).to.include('token must be a jwt string'));

item.name: Reset password - access token is rejected

exec: pm.test('Rejects tokens issued for another purpose', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().message).to.eql('Token is invalid or has expired'));
pm.test('Enforces the password rules', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().message).to.include('password must be longer than or equal to 8 characters'));
pm.test.skip('Set resetToken from the password reset email in the API log', () => {});
pm.test('Reset links are single use', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().message).to.eql('Token is invalid or has expired'));
